clean_story:
"Instant connection. Distance defied. The term quantum entanglement describes particles linked in a way that measuring one instantly reveals the state of another, no matter how far apart.

Most assume signals travel between them. They don’t. Instead, their properties are intertwined from creation, like two coins flipped in opposite rooms landing on the same side every time. In 1935, Einstein called this 'spooky action at a distance,' doubting it could be real. Experiments since the 1970s proved it: entangled photons split by miles still mirror each other’s spin or polarization. Quantum cryptography uses this to create unbreakable codes—any eavesdropper disrupts the link, exposing themselves.

Three related subjects are quantum teleportation, superposition and hidden variables."
